topology_reasoning.what_it_is: A single input access waveguide feeds a wide rectangular multimode interference (MMI) region; self-imaging in the multimode region reproduces the input field as 4 equal images at the far interface, each collected by a tapered output access waveguide. This is a 1x4 MMI splitter (1 in, 4 out).
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Light launched from the bottom single-mode input taper excites many lateral modes of the wide multimode slab (transverse width mmi_width). The modes beat with a length-dependent phase; at the N-fold self-imaging length L = (3*L_pi)/N (N=4) the field forms 4 in-phase images equally spaced across the interface. Tapers at every port expand the single-mode guide (wg_width) up to taper_wide to reduce excess loss / mode mismatch entering and leaving the multimode region.

function_knobs.mmi_length: propagation length of the multimode region (y-extent). Sets the self-imaging condition; THE primary knob that selects 1x4 imaging.
function_knobs.mmi_width: transverse width of the multimode region (x-extent). With mmi_length sets L_pi and the number/position of images.
function_knobs.wg_width: single-mode access waveguide width (mode content of ports).
function_knobs.out_taper_wide / in_taper_wide: port taper width at the MMI interface (mode-matching / loss).
function_knobs.out_taper_length / in_taper_length: adiabaticity of the mode expansion at each port.
function_knobs.out_pitch (port centers): lateral positions of the 4 output images; must equal the MMI self-image spacing = mmi_width/4 offsets.
function_knobs.in_access_length: input single-mode access straight length (mode launch); the knob verified by verify_knob_response (constant-width guide, width=wg_width).

topology_reasoning.orientation_note: Calibration is anisotropic (scale_x=54.88, scale_y=168.2 px/um) because the source figure is portrait but footprint is [25,10] (L=x=25, W=y=10). Geometry is built in GDS coords to fill the 25x10 box so the anisotropic rasterizer overlays the figure; physical aspect is recovered by the stack, not this metric.
